indexes._comment: Requests are queried by denormalised membership so the query matches what firestore.rules authorises (uid in allParticipantIDs). An OR over creatorID/recipientIDs is denied for list queries because Firestore cannot prove every match is readable.
FirestoreRelationshipRepository.fetchRelationships filters by membership and orders by createdAt.
CloudFunctions pendingCountFor() — the push badge is the recipient's real pending count, which needs an array-contains plus an equality.

FirestoreEventRepository.events(forUser:) — equality on userID plus an order on `at` needs a composite index. Without it the query fails FAILED_PRECONDITION, and AdminViewModel swallows that in a `try?`, so the admin Activity section silently reported 'No events recorded' instead of erroring.

fieldOverrides._comment: Usage events are written on every user action and are never read after the reporting window, so without a TTL the collection grows without bound while carrying personal data indefinitely. Firestore deletes each document 90 days after its `at` value. Requires Blaze — under Spark this returns HTTP 403 and fails the whole firestore deploy. The 90-day retention sentence in docs/legal/privacy-policy.md must stay in step with this.
